purpose: One-command regeneration: parameter change -> full regen. Data, not code: flow_graph/param/regen.py executes these stages in manifest order, which must be a valid topological order of depends_on (flow_graph/param/test_regen.py enforces it). Graph-writing stages (writes_graph true) run as a successive-substitution loop until the graph sha is stable. The doc stages then run against the final graph, repeated until none of their outputs change, because some documents read each other (feeds_back_from lists those reverse edges; depends_on holds the forward ones). Stage keys: outputs = files the stage owns; amends = files it rewrites in part (another stage or a person owns the rest); invokes = scripts the stage runs; requires = toolchains it needs ('python:<module>' or 'cmd:<program>'; a missing one skips the stage and vouches nothing); group 'cad' = CAD model builds, run only with regen --cad. not_stages lists every other script that writes files, with its role and reason. flow_graph/test_generators.py fails when a tracked generated file or a file-writing script is not accounted for here.
notes: CORRECTION vs the U3 audit order (verified against code 2026-10-18, commit dc7fe77): _load_list/_one_line moved AFTER the graph writers. U1 (A-M-231) made _power_sizing.py graph-native (it no longer reads the load list), and the U2a sidecars (LOAD_LIST.json/ONE_LINE.json) record the graph sha at run time, so both must run after the last graph write or they vouch an intermediate sha.
CORRECTION: foundry_poly --write runs BEFORE write_graph heat (it stamps FOUNDRY/POLYMERS rates; heat re-solves the ladder against them) and before the balance report.
CORRECTION: _rect_ew_sizing.py is NOT a stage: it writes no doc (stdout JSON only) and is spawned internally by _power_sizing.py, _one_line.py and write_graph.process.

CORRECTION: write_graph power runs LAST among graph writers: _power_sizing demand = max(node continuous_kw, SOL_ARK feed) over every stamp written by the sizing modules, and power then re-stamps PV/ZNBR2/EXT_HALL/mvs.electrical + runs _collection_bus (itself a graph writer).

DECLARED-DAG NOTE: power -> pv_cell_line is a real feedback edge (PV array size sets the cell-line duty; the cell-line kW enters the demand). The manifest declares pv_cell_line -> power only so the dependency graph stays a DAG; regen.py resolves the cycle by looping the writes_graph block to its fixed point (observed: <= 3 passes from a drifted tree, 1 pass from a converged tree).

NOT STAGES: see not_stages (role and reason per script group). flow_graph/param/sanitation.py --write stays a one-time migration (X-SAN-01; sizing/SANITATION.md is classified by-design in _rev_stamp until the module is ported to the current graph).

--quick = the five write_graph stages only (solver + writer what-if mode): no doc regeneration and NO receipt write (a partial run must not clobber the full-run provenance receipt _rev_stamp vouches from).

2026-10-19: balance --write RE-RESTORED (write-convergence fix, same day): the regen acid/base loop had two writer disagreements, not a power<->balance oscillation - (1) the o2_close IA-BMED-04 purge missed the X-PAR-10 spent-return term IA-VS-NAOH (rattle +/-0.0006 kg/d per pass; the write_graph writer always carried it), and (2) the frozen x_par_12_base re-stamps (IA-EVAP_ACID-COND 864.9665, SF-EVAP_ACID, EVAP_ACID node kW) fought the live solver writer (cond 878.7551), a repulsive fixed point that pushed IA-ACID-01 +13.79 kg/d per pass or collapsed it into the IA-BMED-03 -593.49 assert. Fix: D8 single-writer rule in o2_close R10a (write_graph owns solver-solved edges; shared edges derived again through solver.evap on its 4-dp grid behind a 1 g/d epsilon guard) and IA-ACID-01 sized to the leach HCl demand (AQS-DUTY-078 sized-to-draw basis; was a stale +1.57 % over-supply identity fixed point). Standalone settle: 3 passes to a byte-stable sha, moves < 1 g/d after the re-sizing jump; misfit + balance trio green.
2026-10-20: wired nozzle_sched + unit_sizing_sweep into the DAG after duty_basis (their ~195 gated files were only hand-runnable before).

2026-10-24: every generator unified into this manifest: the document generators that were run by hand became doc stages, the inventory, PLC-program and code-basis builders became stages, o2_source became a stage (its frozen Rev A input is read from the rewritten history commit), and the CAD builds became the 'cad' group. _rev_stamp reads its derived-file set from this manifest.

stages.name: balance_report
stages.note: 2026-10-21: balance --write proven stable at the balanced writer set. Evidence: instrumented 4-pass probe (PV_ARRAY count 4982, SOL_ARK count 35, sections 4, IA-PV-01 336.7016, need 179.62 kW) is pass-invariant; suite 43/43; regen --check rc=0. Diagnostic recipe if cycles reappear: capture per-pass signature hashes (graph sha + pv/ark/sections counts + pv feeder) over >=3 full passes BEFORE reverting - a quantized threshold flip (breaker/kVA tables) shows as a 2-point signature cycle, not a random walk. The 2026-10-19 oscillation report did not reproduce at this writer set.

not_stages.reason: The pipeline runner itself, and its locale runner (--site), which writes only under sites/<site_id>/.

Imported by stages (closure_tf by balance_report; stable_ids by the inventory stages, which own the *_family_ids.json registers; the models/freecad modules by build_plant.py under cad_freecad). A command-line entry point, where present, rewrites files a stage already owns.
Design-tool server code: writes user sandboxes and export packs at run time, not repository files.
Writes an untracked preview PNG beside the script. The sheets published in media/pfd are run by stage regen_derived.
Prints the evidence for a dated study page; writes no repository file.
One-time edit of the graph, already applied; the graph is the authority now. Re-running would rewrite the graph, and several no longer match it.
Layout tools. They seed or move rows in the placement files, which were refined after the tool ran, so the placement files are inputs; re-running would discard that work.

Repository checks run by tests (flow_graph/test_citations.py, flow_graph/test_doc_style.py). They write files only when asked to (check_citations --fix rewrites stale citations; check_doc_style --shrink drops clean pages from the pending list), so they are not regeneration stages.
